title: Child Safeguarding: Suspected Non-Accidental Injury Assessment and Referral

evidenceAudit.scope: Recognition, immediate safety, objective documentation and referral when non-accidental injury is suspected.
findings: The named primary guideline was opened and the cited sections were used.
Normal values are descriptive; use local laboratory and age/pregnancy ranges.
unverifiedSections: No topic-specific Saudi national guideline was identified in the opened Saudi MOH protocol index.
SFDA registration and hospital formulary availability were not verified; no drug dose is supplied.

pathophysiology.summary: Inflicted injury may produce patterns inconsistent with developmental ability or the account given. Repeated harm can coexist with neglect, emotional abuse or coercive family dynamics. Unsafe discharge can expose the child or siblings to further harm.
keyMechanisms: Inflicted injury may produce patterns inconsistent with developmental ability or the account given.
Repeated harm can coexist with neglect, emotional abuse or coercive family dynamics.
Unsafe discharge can expose the child or siblings to further harm.

references.title: NICE NG76: Child abuse and neglect

symptoms: Pain, bleeding, altered behaviour, fearfulness or a disclosure by the child.
physicalSigns: Injury inconsistent with history or development, patterned injury, multiple ages of injury, concerning interaction or unmet basic needs.
redFlags: Immediate danger, serious injury, suspected abusive head trauma, strangulation, sexual assault, poisoning, weapon injury or threats to the child.
precipitants: No single family factor proves abuse; assess the child, history, development and context without stereotyping.

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Mechanism, injury and developmental ability are consistent.
Medical condition may contribute but does not automatically exclude inflicted harm.
Seek safeguarding expertise; harmful practice still requires protection.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: If maltreatment is suspected, refer to the local child-protection service; immediate danger requires emergency safeguarding/police action (NG76 sections 1.2–1.4).

ruleIn.testName: Separate, verbatim history and developmental assessment
ruleIn.expectedFinding: Inconsistent, changing or implausible account; delay in presentation
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Document who said what and when; avoid leading questions.

references.title: NICE NG76: Child abuse and neglect

ruleIn.expectedFinding: Patterned, protected-site, multiple or age-incongruent injuries
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Use body maps and approved clinical photography with policy and consent/legal basis.

references.title: NICE NG76: Child abuse and neglect

ruleOut.expectedFinding: Occult fracture, intracranial injury, retinal injury or internal trauma
ruleOut.clinicalRationale: A safeguarding paediatrician selects tests by age and presentation; do not use an indiscriminate panel.

references.title: NICE NG76: Child abuse and neglect

clinicalManagement.title: Treat injury and secure safety
actions: Treat life threats and relieve pain while preserving forensic evidence where relevant.
Do not discharge to a person or place considered unsafe.

clinicalManagement.title: Document objectively
actions: Record verbatim disclosure, separate accounts, timing, development, examination and diagrams.
Share only necessary information through the authorised safeguarding pathway.

clinicalManagement.title: Escalate and refer
actions: Contact the named safeguarding lead/paediatrician and statutory child-protection service according to local law and policy.
Consider siblings and other children who may be at risk; document the named accepting professional and safety plan.

medicationPlan.note: Treat injuries and symptoms through their clinical pathways; there is no medicine pathway for safeguarding assessment.

teaching.scope: Recognition, immediate safety, objective documentation and referral when non-accidental injury is suspected.
learningObjectives: Recognise the condition and its red flags.
Choose initial tests without delaying urgent escalation.
Use a named multidisciplinary disposition plan.
keyPoints: Immediate danger, serious injury, suspected abusive head trauma, strangulation, sexual assault, poisoning, weapon injury or threats to the child.
Contact the named safeguarding lead/paediatrician and statutory child-protection service according to local law and policy.
pitfalls: Delaying escalation while waiting for non-essential tests.
Using an unverified medicine regimen instead of the current local protocol.

references.title: NICE NG76: Child abuse and neglect

patientEducation: Explain the working diagnosis, immediate plan and specific return or deterioration signs.
lifestyleAndDiet: Address prevention and self-management only after the acute safety plan is complete.
dischargeCriteria: Medical needs treated and an explicit multiagency safety decision recorded; never discharge solely because the accompanying adult requests it.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Ensure handover, statutory referral outcome, forensic/paediatric follow-up and support for the child are closed-loop.
